newsitem.title: USA: Chronimed shares down on supply problem.
newsitem.headline: Chronimed shares down on supply problem.

text.p: Shares in Chronimed Inc fell 2-1/8 to 12-7/8 on Wednesday after the company said its supplier of test strips for its Quik Check blood glucose monitor temporarily halted shipment.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has raised questions about the consistency of the strips' test results and shipment was voluntarily stopped in late December, said medical technology analyst Ann Logue at Volpe Welty.
"If they don't get shipment, then (Chronimed) is going to have down earnings in the March quarter," Logue said.

In a statement accompanying fiscal second quarter financial results released Tuesday, Chronimed chief executive Maurice Taylor said: "Chronimed's strip supplier and independent experts in the field of diabetes have disputed the FDA's preliminary findings in their test. Our supplier has been working very closely with the FDA on this matter.
"Pending resolution of the dispute, we remain cautiously optimistic about the timing of resuming shipments of the Quick Check."
Chronimed executives could not immediately be reached Wednesday for further comment.
The strip supplier is privately held Diagnostic Solutions Inc, of Irvine, Calif., Logue said.
In 1995, Diagnostic temporarily halted strip production to work on improving efficiency and product quality. The halt hurt Chronimed's fiscal third quarter that year.
"In my opinion, there's a question as to why management is even in this buisness when there's evidence that this supplier is somewhat unreliable," Logue said.
Minneapolis-based Chronimed sells products and services to people suffering from chronic diseases, such as diabetes, HIV/AIDS and other disorders.
